analysis: Examined three changes. (1) ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.swift head 46-48: discoveryMode no longer forces `.off` under `auto` for coordinator setups when the build declares a public assistant. readAutomatic (head ~132-149) takes `declared` from ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant(for: capability)?.policy only when coordinator=true. It passes the declared depth and verification arguments to the native helper, and requireDiscoveredQuote (head ~110-120) requires exact policy equality with the declaration. This is stricter than the old depth/admittedCohort check. Local, undeclared and `on` paths match base behaviour. (2) DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift head 668-678: publicTrafficLine now defaults to ClusterPublicModels.current, not .declared. It suppresses the tensorAssistantNotOffered line when the artifact has a declared assistant. This function is display/onboarding text only. ownerServing (651) still uses `.declared`. The grant, requireRank, plannable and startRefusal logic is unchanged. (3) ClusterApprovalAttachment.swift head 135-138 changes only a comment. It now says the build-pinned resource_policy_sha256 (already compared at line 26) carries the declared resident assistant. Security relevance: the PR allows Qwen speculative-assistant decoding to be offered for public/coordinator traffic when the build declares it. Before, the base comment said it had no parity qualification. This touches output-integrity assumptions (T-007, T-056) and TB-011 qualification. Actual enforcement is in ClusterConfiguration.validate/tensorAssistantServesLocally and ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant/current, and none of these were supplied. Integration should verify four things. (a) validate refuses any coordinator-paired setup whose assistant policy differs from the declaration. (b) `current` and `declared` cannot diverge so that the UI line overstates public qualification. (c) The coordinator's parity qualification still covers assistant placements. (d) The declaration is bound to the artifact SHA and cannot be operator-supplied. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied source.
